summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the circuit court erred by treating the mother's stipulation as an adjudication binding the father and by denying him an adjudicatory hearing, but affirmed the termination because on this record the error was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt.
key_cases.relevance: This is the controlling South Dakota statement that filing a petition triggers an adjudicatory hearing for every non-admitting parent under SDCL 26-7A-55.
key_cases.quote: the court could only dispense with an adjudicatory hearing if all of the necessary parties, including the father, agreed

key_cases.case_name: People ex rel. South Dakota Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that the circuit court erred in letting an indigent mother proceed pro se at the adjudicatory hearing without the procedures that safeguard the SDCL 26-7A-31 right to counsel, but found the error harmless on the facts and affirmed termination.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the statutory right to appointed counsel that attaches to parents once a petition is filed and an adjudicatory hearing is set.
key_cases.quote: SDCL 26-7A-31 specifically provides for a court appointed attorney for parents in an abuse and neglect proceeding.

key_cases.case_name: Lassiter v. Department of Social Services of Durham County
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that due process does not require appointed counsel in every parental termination proceeding and left the appointment decision to the trial court case by case, subject to appellate review, finding no error in the refusal to appoint counsel there.
key_cases.relevance: It is the federal baseline for the right to counsel in dependency and termination proceedings, against which South Dakota's broader statutory right under SDCL 26-7A-31 should be read.
key_cases.quote: neither can we say that the Constitution requires the appointment of counsel in every parental termination proceeding

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the adjudication and termination, holding that the State proved abuse and neglect by clear and convincing evidence and that DSS need not exhaust every possible form of assistance before termination becomes the least restrictive alternative.
key_cases.relevance: It states the evidentiary burden the State carries once it files the petition and proceeds to the adjudicatory hearing.
key_cases.quote: The State has the burden of proving that the children were abused or neglected by clear and convincing evidence.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment forbids a State from terminating parental rights on a mere preponderance of the evidence and requires proof by at least clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: It is the federal constitutional floor that shapes what the State must ultimately be prepared to prove once it files a petition aimed at severance.
key_cases.quote: due process requires that the State support its allegations by at least clear and convincing evidence

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an adjudication of abuse and neglect and termination of the father's parental rights, holding that the State proved abuse and neglect by clear and convincing evidence on the parents' history with their other children and that termination was the least restrictive alternative.
key_cases.relevance: It is the customary South Dakota primary citation for the clear-and-convincing burden and the standard of review that attach once the State files its abuse and neglect petition, and it is the authority In re S.A. cites on that point.
key_cases.quote: Termination of parental rights is proper only when the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that termination is the least restrictive alternative in keeping with the child's best interest.
